bullets.text: Q2 CR was 92.7 (YTD 91.8); Commercial Auto CR 89.6 (YTD under 89); net income fell to $212M, down YOY almost exclusively on a $55M negative realized investment delta.

Bodily injury frequency and severity declined; prior-year reserve downward adjustments totaled $33.6M ($72.7M YTD); collision frequency continued falling with severity near flat; personal injury trends moderated in frequency and severity.
Repurchased 3.3M shares; paid ~$2M to terminate a debt covenant and retired ~$223M hybrid debt at 95 cents on the dollar; debt-to-capital reached 25.7%; YTD return was 3.1%.
Written premium grew 5% in Q2, accelerating monthly from 4% to 6%; performance felt acceptable in the current environment; Commercial Auto saw selective return to growth across some segments.

Agency operations showed renewed strength with results tracking nicely; Direct operations continued posting very attractive numbers, and measures suggested strong consumer acceptance of brand messaging and product features.
Rolling out latest Personal Lines product design across Agency and Direct; releasing a repackaged UBI initiative designed to capture essential data while eliminating potential consumer concerns.

Wisconsin took center stage in new application demand when mandatory insurance began June 1st; Progressive welcomed many new customers, noting this external demand influence was a one-time change not expected often.

Management believes underperforming states subject to corrective actions are moving toward normalized operations; reserve adjustments for bodily injury require severity estimation caution without a compelling thesis explaining why negative trends would continue.
Through the half year, the Gainshare score was 1.51 out of 2.0; the measure serves as the core element of all variable cash compensation at every level and for shareholder variable dividends.
Expects the combination of growth and underwriting profit will place Progressive among the leading few peers, if not setting the pace, once second-quarter competitor results are published.
